The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Kalshi off-limits in multiple states as prediction markets, CFTC team up for battle. Washington state is cut off for Kalshi customers while the company combats the development in court and its federal regulator keeps pursuing new rules. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin and Ether bears get decimated amid 'squeeze-led' rally and Musk's X wants to pay creators in stablecoins: Crypto's week in 5 stories. Bitcoin and crypto staged their strongest rally in months as Treasury intervention, regulatory moves and a historic short squeeze collided, while banks and technology companies pushed deeper into stablecoins. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Zcash jumps 48% to over $800 as Grayscale spot ETF push adds to ‘next bitcoin’ buzz. ZEC traded above its January 2018 peak as futures volume hit billions of dollars and a Grayscale filing showed fresh progress toward converting its Zcash Trust into a spot ETF. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

How a Treasury buyback tweak helped bitcoin surge 25% to nearly $80,000 in days. Treasury buybacks are not QE, analysts said, but the move helped pull long-term yields off 19-year highs and triggered a record short squeeze in a market already leaning too bearish. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto advocates join in suing Illinois over digital asset tax. The Crypto Council for Innovation and the Blockchain Association added another lawsuit against the state for its recently approved 0.2% crypto tax. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Pass the Clarity Act. Reopening a settled provision four weeks before a vote would sink the bill, argues Summer Mersinger, CEO of the Blockchain Association. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,224 with a -0.47% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,428.18 with a +1.13% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On September 19, 2025, Treasury issued an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

Read more on Latham's Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’s Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

items.title: Geopolitical conflict and its impact on global markets - U.S. Bank
items.description: Geopolitics refer to events that influence the global landscape, including political or trade tensions and military conflicts. Such events often create economic uncertainty, which can lead to fluctuations in stock prices, interest rates, and currencies. Geopolitical conflicts frequently impact supply chains, such as Iran’s threats to halt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Wars in agricultural regions can also affect crop yields and deliveries. Events like these can cause supply-demand [...] History does not guarantee a quick recovery from every geopolitical shock, and markets can remain volatile when conflict disrupts essential supplies or broadens into the economy. Still, investors have often moved past the first wave of selling once they could assess the likely effects on growth, inflation and profits. A diversified portfolio and a clear investment plan can help investors participate when markets recover from the early negative impacts of major geopolitical events. [...] International markets face greater potential pressure because many European and Asian economies import a larger share of the energy they consume. The United States produces more of its own energy, but higher global prices still raise costs for American households and businesses. Recent market resilience does not eliminate geopolitical risk; it shows that investors continue to weigh conflict against the economy’s ability to absorb disruption.
